Annotation Interface RegionalByRow

@Documented @Retention(RUNTIME) @Target(TYPE) public @interface RegionalByRow
Declares that the annotated entity's table should have the CockroachDB REGIONAL BY ROW locality — each row is homed in a region (its crdb_region value) so that region's nodes own the leaseholder and reads/writes from there are fast. Per-user or per-tenant data is the usual candidate.

This annotation is declared intent only: it does not change the schema. Your migrations still own ALTER TABLE ... SET LOCALITY REGIONAL BY ROW, and that statement rewrites the table. Pair it with Crdb.verifyLocality(DataSource, Class...) to check, at an explicit point you choose, that the live table matches the annotation (and to get the exact fix-up SQL when it does not).

Mark the field mapped to the region column with CrdbRegion so the check knows which column homes the rows; or name the column directly with regionColumn(). With neither, CockroachDB's implicit crdb_region column is assumed.

An entity must not carry both @RegionalByRow and GlobalTable; that is a contradiction the check always reports.

Table-name resolution follows the same rule and the same one limitation as GlobalTable.table(): the simple class name folded to lower case, no snake_case conversion; override with table().

  • Element Details

    • table

      String table
      The table this entity maps to, optionally schema-qualified and/or quoted. Empty (the default) means the entity's simple class name, folded to lower case. See GlobalTable.table() for the resolution rules.
      Default:
      ""

    • regionColumn

      String regionColumn
      The name of the region column that homes each row. Empty (the default) means: use the column of the CrdbRegion-annotated field if there is one, otherwise CockroachDB's implicit crdb_region. Set this when the region column is not represented by a field. Folded to lower case like any unquoted identifier.
      Default:
      ""
